title: Home
metaDescription: Sell your West Virginia mineral or royalty interest to a buyer who reviews your title chain and production history before making an offer.
heroLead: West Virginia mineral titles are old, often fractional, and frequently tangled in heirship that was never fully resolved at the courthouse, and that is exactly the kind of file we work through every week.
intro: If you own mineral or royalty rights somewhere in West Virginia, chances are the interest reached you through a chain of deeds and inheritances stretching back further than a single generation. Maybe it is a fractional share that came down through a grandparent's estate. Maybe it is an old flat-rate lease that has paid the same fixed sum for years while a well nearby has clearly done better than that. Maybe you simply want an honest read on what a producing or unleased interest is actually worth before deciding whether to sell.

We buy West Virginia mineral and royalty interests directly, and we do the title work up front rather than after the fact, which means fewer surprises for you and a faster path to closing when the ownership picture is clear.

sections.heading: How we approach a West Virginia file
paragraphs: West Virginia mineral estates were severed from the surface decades ago in a huge number of tracts, and the resulting ownership record is often thinner than a family assumes. Before we make an offer, we look at the actual chain of title: the original severance or conveyance deed, any subsequent transfers, and how ownership passed through any estates along the way. This is not a formality for us, it is how we arrive at a number that reflects what you actually own and can convey.

We also look closely at production history where it exists, pulling royalty statements and division order decimals rather than relying on a single check or a rough county-wide assumption. A well several years into its decline behaves differently than one still ramping, and that difference matters to any honest valuation.

sections.heading: Flat-rate leases and what they mean for your offer
paragraphs: West Virginia has a substantial number of older leases still on the books that pay a flat annual sum rather than a percentage of production, some of them decades old and unchanged since they were signed. If your family has been receiving the same lease payment year after year regardless of what the well produces, that flat-rate structure is very likely suppressing your near-term income relative to what the underlying acreage would support under a modern royalty lease. We look at exactly this gap when we evaluate flat-rate acreage, and we account for it in how we structure an offer rather than pricing solely off the current lease payment.

sections.heading: Fractional and heirship interests
paragraphs: A large share of the files we see involve an interest that passed down through inheritance to several siblings, cousins, or more distant relatives, sometimes without ever being formally probated or documented at the county clerk's office. This is common across West Virginia and it does not disqualify you from selling. It usually just means an extra curative step, such as an affidavit of heirship or a corrective deed, needs to happen alongside the sale. We work through that process directly with you rather than asking you to sort it out on your own first.

sections.heading: What to expect if you reach out
paragraphs: We start with a conversation about what you own, whatever documents you already have on hand, and whether your interest is currently leased, producing, or entirely undeveloped. From there we do our own title review, put together an offer that reflects your specific tract rather than a generic county estimate, and walk with you through any curative paperwork your file requires. There is no obligation to move forward at any point in that process.

faqs.question: Do you buy mineral rights that are not currently producing?
faqs.answer: Yes. We evaluate unleased and non-producing mineral interests based on nearby drilling and leasing activity, play position, and the tract's title history, in addition to producing interests with an active royalty history.

faqs.question: What if my family never formally probated the estate the minerals came through?
faqs.answer: This is common in West Virginia and is usually resolvable with an affidavit of heirship or similar curative document. We help walk through what specific step your file needs rather than asking you to figure it out alone.

faqs.question: I only own a small fractional share inherited with several cousins. Can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can generally sell your own undivided fractional share independently of what other heirs decide to do with theirs, as long as your share can be documented back to the recorded chain of title.

faqs.question: How do you value an interest under an old flat-rate lease?
faqs.answer: We look at the gap between what the flat-rate lease currently pays and what the acreage would likely support under current production or leasing activity nearby, and we factor that difference into the offer rather than pricing off the flat payment alone.

faqs.question: Is there any cost or obligation to get an offer?
faqs.answer: No. There is no cost to have your interest reviewed, and you are under no obligation to sell if the offer does not work for you.
